problem: Diffusion Bridge and Flow Matching are two competing approaches for transforming between arbitrary distributions, but their relative merits and practical applicability remain unclear due to different modeling assumptions and implementations.
approach: Unified analysis through Stochastic Optimal Control and Optimal Transport perspectives, with a Transformer-based latent architecture enabling fair empirical comparison across image restoration, translation, and style transfer tasks.
contribution: Proved that Diffusion Bridge has lower cost function for stable trajectories and Flow Matching becomes ineffective at reduced data sizes; comprehensive experiments validate theoretical predictions across varying distributional difficulty and data size.

problem: Existing geometric deep learning methods only exploit certain symmetry structures; richer symmetries in data that could improve performance and efficiency remain unexploited.
approach: Develop order-equivariant neural networks (OENN) generalizing graph message passing and sheaf neural networks through equivariant bundles over face posets, with universal approximation theorems for continuous order-equivariant maps.
contribution: First universal approximation theorem for sheaf neural networks; OENN framework subsumes and extends graph neural networks while enabling leverage of categorical symmetries including non-invertible symmetries with compositional relations.

problem: Softmax attention enforces strict unit-sum normalization that limits flexibility in controlling attention magnitudes and can lead to overly concentrated or unstable attention patterns during training.
approach: Introduce Affine-Scaled Attention adding input-dependent scaling and bias terms to softmax-normalized weights, relaxing normalization constraints while maintaining value aggregation and allowing controlled attention reweighting.
contribution: Large-scale LLM pretraining experiments show consistent improvements in training stability, optimization behavior, and downstream task performance compared to standard softmax attention and attention sink baselines.

problem: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is difficult due to sparse signals and severe experimental noise, with existing methods suffering from mean collapse that produces false positives by predicting global averages.
approach: AdaPert uses differentiable node selection to extract sparse perturbation-specific subgraphs, suppressing spurious variation in non-responsive genes while emphasizing differentially expressed ones.
contribution: Outperforms existing baselines across multiple benchmarks with largest gains on DEG-aware metrics by extracting perturbation-specific knowledge rather than treating biological knowledge graphs as dense static priors.

problem: Text-to-Audio-Video generation evaluation is fragmented, relying on coarse embedding similarity that fails to capture fine-grained joint correctness required for realistic multi-modal prompts.
approach: AVGen-Bench proposes a multi-granular evaluation framework combining specialist models with Multimodal LLMs, assessing audio-video generation across 11 real-world categories from perceptual quality to semantic controllability.
contribution: Benchmark reveals significant gap between strong audio-visual aesthetics and weak semantic reliability, with persistent failures in text rendering, speech coherence, physical reasoning, and universal breakdown in musical pitch control.

problem: Existing LLM-based kernel optimization methods struggle with semantic mismatch between generalized reasoning and low-level system behaviors, suffering from runtime blindness and configuration fragmentation.
approach: QiMeng-PerceptOS shifts to perception-driven tuning integrating: (1) Perception Module aligning telemetry into semantic fingerprints, (2) Bi-level Hierarchical Induction Tree for efficient search, (3) Posterior Enhancement suppressing hallucinations via trajectory synthesis.
contribution: Achieves 296.6% of default Redis throughput and surpasses SOTA by 32.6% within 15 iterations, establishing perception-driven closed-loop for automated system optimization.

problem: Large reasoning models require expensive full-precision inference and suffer from high KV cache footprints; full 4-bit FP4 quantization causes severe reasoning degradation that existing methods cannot recover.
approach: ReQAT proposes reasoning-centric FP4 training with Trace-Aligned QAT revisiting identical reasoning traces, Selective Entropy Minimization reinforcing low-entropy positions, and Q-FIT initialization calibrating RoPE-consistent KV cache.
contribution: Recovers and surpasses BF16 accuracy under same training budget while delivering up to 3.9x throughput speedup on NVIDIA DGX Spark and 3.1x on B200.

problem: While RL algorithm design drives recent reasoning model progress, data scheduling decisions that determine training data over time remain underexplored despite being critical for competitive code generation.
approach: DRIVE pipeline with hardness-prioritized SFT and two-stage RL: first stage uses decreased max sequence length to expand entropy, second stage uses large rollouts per prompt and curriculum design for exploration.
contribution: Achieves sota for 32B models in competitive code generation on LeetCode and Codeforces weekly contests; implementation on Qwen2.5-32B and 389B MoE model demonstrates effectiveness and scalability.

problem: Existing gradient-based sufficient dimension reduction estimators either suffer from curse of dimensionality in ambient space or incur quadratic per-iteration cost when localizing to reduced space.
approach: SMAVE recasts MAVE risk as smooth maximization on Stiefel manifold with closed-form Riemannian gradient, combining sparse projected-space nearest-neighbor localization with Riemannian stochastic gradient ascent.
contribution: Almost-sure convergence with non-asymptotic rate matching standard non-convex first-order scaling; matches or improves synthetic subspace recovery at high dimension and uniformly outperforms OPG with orders of magnitude lower runtime.

problem: The Mountain Car problem, a canonical RL benchmark for 36 years, lacks analytical optimal solution, hindering understanding of why modern RL agents display large gaps to optimality.
approach: Analytically solve Mountain Car to derive optimal control, then introduce Chebyshev policies as universal dense class of RL policies from first principles, trainable as neural net drop-in replacements.
contribution: Chebyshev policies reduce regret by factor of 4.18 while requiring 277 times fewer parameters; consistent improvements on further RL tasks and real-world nonlinear motion control testbed, demonstrating sample efficiency and explainability.

problem: Existing multimodal federated learning methods assume homogeneous models and balanced modality distributions, ill-suited for practical scenarios with heterogeneous client architectures and severe modality imbalance.
approach: MFedPBA framework with dual alignment mechanism: feature-level alignment via projection encoder using contrastive learning and Gromov-Wasserstein distance, and decision-level alignment via entropy-weighted logit prototype aggregation.
contribution: Significantly outperforms sota baselines under model heterogeneity and modality imbalance conditions through joint handling of heterogeneous feature spaces and collective decision aggregation.

problem: The emerging Agentic Web paradigm shifts from centralized information retrieval to decentralized coordination, but how well autonomous agents can synthesize answers by interacting with content-specific agents remains unexplored.
approach: AgentWebBench evaluates user agent synthesis across four information-need tasks (web search, recommendation, QA, deep research) with seven LLMs and three coordination strategies in decentralized settings.
contribution: Multi-agent coordination lags centralized retrieval as expected but gap shrinks with model scale; decentralized access concentrates traffic, test-time scaling improves performance, and strong results require careful planning and sufficient interactions.

problem: Standard LLM-as-a-Judge protocols systematically fail when evaluating upper-undergraduate to early graduate level mathematics proofs, showing significant biases and reasoning disparities.
approach: QEDBench introduces first benchmark systematically measuring alignment with human experts on undergraduate proofs, contrasting course-specific rubrics against expert common knowledge via dual-evaluation matrix (7 judges × 5 solvers) on 1,000+ hours.
contribution: Reveals frontier evaluators like Claude 4.5 Opus exhibit positive bias up to +0.28, while specialized reasoning models like o3-deep-research collapse in discrete domains (42.1% accuracy in Graph Theory vs 0.91 for generalists.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models suffer significant performance drops when encountering unseen real-world visual disturbances absent from training data, limiting practical robustness.
approach: StableVLA proposes Information Bottleneck Adapter (IB-Adapter) module grounded in information theory that selectively filters noise from visual inputs without requiring extra data or augmentation, improves over baseline average 30%.
contribution: With negligible parameter overhead (<10M), achieves robustness competitive with 7B sota VLAs despite using 14x smaller backbone (0.5B) and no Open X-Embodiment pretraining; maintains accuracy on long-horizon tasks and surpasses OpenPi under disturbances.

problem: Existing LMM-based image quality assessment methods support only partial perception dimensions (reasoning or pixel-level grounding), lacking unified frameworks for multi-granularity quality understanding.
approach: IQA-Spider formulates four-task paradigm (global/local description, pixel-level grounding, region-level referring) with scalable automatic annotation and conflict-free two-stage design progressively extending text-level understanding to pixel-level grounding.
contribution: Achieves unified multi-granularity explainable image quality assessment across multiple benchmarks through training-free text-to-point grounding paradigm mapping token logits to spatial coordinates.

problem: Mainstream distributed RL frameworks rely on centralized architecture coupling control dispatch with data transmission, creating significant communication bottlenecks that severely limit scalability and efficiency for LLM post-training.
approach: DistFlow adopts fully distributed multi-controller paradigm decoupling data from control, with parallelism-aware Data Coordinator leveraging local caching and load balancing, plus DAG-based task scheduler for fine-grained independent execution.
contribution: Achieves near-linear scalability up to 512 GPUs with up to 2.63x throughput improvement over sota frameworks for distributed RL at scale.

problem: Omni-modal LLMs relying on long multimodal token sequences suffer substantial computational overhead; token compression methods designed for omni-modals remain limited.
approach: OmniSIFT proposes two-stage compression: (i) spatio-temporal video pruning removing intra-frame and inter-frame redundancy, (ii) vision-guided audio selection filtering tokens, optimized end-to-end via differentiable straight-through estimator.
contribution: With only 25% of original token context and 4.85M added parameters, consistently outperforms compression baselines and surpasses full-token model on several tasks for Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.

problem: Prompt learning for vision-language models suffers fundamental bottleneck: sample-wise optimization within task-specific feature spaces traps models in local optima, hindering global optimality.
approach: AlignedNorm identifies Coupled Prompt Field as shared space where base and new tasks are mutually constrained, enforcing field coupling by dynamically aligning prompt norms to VLM native scale for joint optimization.
contribution: Without complex designs, matches leading decoupled approaches on 15 datasets across 4 settings, offering new perspective and practical solution to local-optima dilemma in prompt learning.

problem: Building multimodal Transformers on Spiking Neural Networks is hindered by unstable training in deep spiking stacks and mismatch between dense softmax attention and spike-based communication.
approach: SMM Transformer combines: (i) Parallel LIF neuron with Multistage Learnable Parameters and P-STBP algorithm for training stability, (ii) spike-driven attention approximation with lightweight self-compensation, (iii) spiking mixture-of-experts for modality fusion.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracy vs ANN baselines while reducing estimated compute energy of attention module up to 97% under standard MAC/AC cost model on visual and multimodal benchmarks.

problem: GFlowNets for molecular generation must truncate trajectory length in vast chemical space, conflating incomplete fragments with valid molecules and distorting learned distribution.
approach: LeakGFN uses dual-head architecture decomposing flow into: chemical head modeling full space and valid head estimating reachability fraction, with valid head implicitly learning molecular accessibility.
contribution: Proves LeakGFN recovers correct distribution over accessible molecules under mild assumptions; achieves sota on 4 of 5 molecular optimization tasks with plug-and-play integration into existing frameworks.

problem: Existing online change-point detection methods rely on fixed-dimensional Euclidean summaries, obscuring important changes in distributional shape or geometry.
approach: Proposes intrinsic distribution-valued CPD treating streaming batch data as stochastic process on 2-Wasserstein space, mapping distributions to tangent space relative to pre-change Fréchet barycenter for reference-centered linearization.
contribution: Detects complex distributional shifts with reduced detection delay at matched ARL0 compared with moments-based and model-free baselines through sequential detectors on tangent fields.

problem: Multimodal models face two obstacles: collecting large-scale paired datasets is impractical, and existing representations entangle shared and modality-specific information, hindering interpretability.
approach: MultiLoReFT extends low-rank adaptation to multimodal setting with pretrained unimodal models, learning interpretable projection subspaces that decouple shared and modality-specific information.
contribution: Produces multimodal representations supporting prediction while explicitly revealing distributed shared and modality-specific information across modalities on simulated and real-world benchmarks.

problem: Evolutionary multi-view classification assumes noise-free training labels, but label noise introduces fitness evaluation bias that misguides evolutionary search toward local optima.
approach: GFD-EMVC proposes detect-then-calibrate data purification using outlier analysis in gradient space to identify noisy samples and prototype calibration in feature space to correct labels.
contribution: Effectively purifies data and alleviates fitness evaluation bias, improving performance of various multi-view learning paradigms in label noise scenarios.

problem: Continual learning with pre-trained models faces critical challenges like catastrophic forgetting and parameter interference without historical data, with existing methods overlooking loss landscape sharpness and singular value alignment.
approach: SAIM framework with Sharpness-Aware Block Coordinate Descent optimizer guiding toward flatter minima and adaptive isotropic merging balancing singular value spectrum across tasks.
contribution: Achieves 5-10% higher accuracy than existing methods while maintaining robust performance as task count increases, with code available.

problem: Aligning LLMs to heterogeneous and rapidly evolving safety requirements remains critical; existing instruction-tuned models and standalone classifiers fail to generalize to new safety configurations.
approach: CSRM jointly optimizes calibrated safety compliance and reward modeling with configuration-targeted data augmentation enforcing instruction adherence while preserving severity structure.
contribution: Achieves sota on CoSApien (94.6% F1) and DynaBench (75.8% F1) without additional annotation; yields downstream LLMs with improved helpfulness-safety tradeoff when used for safety alignment.

problem: Video predictive models for robotics operate on 2D sequences, inherently lacking 3D geometric understanding necessary for precise spatial reasoning and physical consistency.
approach: Structured 4D Latent Predictive Model predicts evolution of scene 3D structure in structured latent space conditioned on observations and textual instructions, decodable into diverse 3D formats.
contribution: Generates futures with strong visual quality and substantially better 3D consistency and multi-view coherence vs sota video-based planners; achieves superior manipulation performance with robust generalization to novel conditions.

problem: Bridging sim2real gap between inexpensive models and complex physical systems remains central challenge, especially in multi-scale settings where reduced-order models capture only dominant dynamics.
approach: Cheap2Rich combines fast low-fidelity prior with learned interpretable discrepancy corrections via multi-scale data assimilation, demonstrated on rotating detonation engines coupling detonation-front, injector effects, and stiff chemistry.
contribution: Successfully reconstructs high-fidelity RDE states from sparse measurements while isolating physically meaningful discrepancy dynamics, providing general framework for complex multi-scale systems.

problem: While continuous-time RL shows empirical success, its instance-dependent behavior and ability to adapt to varying problem difficulty remain poorly understood.
approach: Develop model-based algorithm built on maximum likelihood estimation estimating state marginal density rather than dynamics directly, with randomized measurement schedule adapting to problem complexity.
contribution: Establishes instance-dependent regret bound scaling with total reward variance and measurement resolution; regret becomes independent of measurement strategy when observation frequency adapts appropriately.

problem: Decentralized optimization requires both resilience against Byzantine attackers and faster convergence on sparse networks, but existing methods fail to achieve both simultaneously.
approach: BRED integrates Byzantine-robust Exact Diffusion within scaled dual ascent framework, mitigating error accumulation; momentum variant BRED-M further reduces complexity.
contribution: Achieves linear speedup with transient complexity O((1-λ)^-2) and Byzantine-affected complexity reduced from O(δ²(1-λ)^-6) to O(δ²(1-λ)^-4), demonstrated on benchmark datasets.

problem: Training transformers that behave like optimization descent algorithms typically uses standard empirical risk minimization without enforcing monotonic loss decrease across layers.
approach: Introduce constrained optimization framework enforcing layerwise descent constraints on objective and replacing ERM with primal-dual training scheme yielding intermediate representations decreasing loss monotonically.
contribution: Constrained transformers achieve stronger robustness to perturbations and maintain higher out-of-distribution generalization while preserving competitive in-distribution performance on video denoising and text classification.

problem: Sparse Autoencoders extract LLM features with hyperparameter L0 (average firing features per token) treated as free parameter, but incorrect L0 causes SAE feature disentanglement failures.
approach: Study L0 effects showing too-low L0 mixes features for reconstruction while too-high L0 finds degenerate mixing solutions; present proxy metric guiding L0 search using toy models and sparse probing.
contribution: Most commonly used SAEs have L0 too low; practitioners must set L0 correctly to train monosemantic SAEs, with proxy metric helping find correct value on given distribution.

problem: Recent work shows vanilla transformer context impact via rank-1 MLP weight patches, but generalization to modern LLM architectures with diverse components remains uncharacterized.
approach: Provide precise analytical solution for Gemma-style blocks mapping entire context effect to rank-1 MLP patches and RMSNorm scale patches, generalizing via framework centered on input/output controllability.
contribution: Proves perfect implicit weight patch possible for any MLP block with input-controllable inner and output-controllable outer functions, extending to gating, norms, mixture of experts, and sequential/parallel blocks.

problem: Point cloud registration faces distinct challenges in rigid vs non-rigid settings due to multi-scale discrepancy between global transformation consistency and local deformation, resisting unified approaches.
approach: RGGT uses generative-prior-guided Transformer with coordinated design across representation, architecture, and supervision: generative priors enrich features, Global-Self-Cross Attention models multi-scale reasoning, dual objective provides consistent supervision.
contribution: Achieves sota accuracy on rigid (ModelNet40, 3DMatch, KITTI) and non-rigid (4DMatch) benchmarks within single unified framework, demonstrating multi-scale geometric-semantic capture.

problem: Offline multi-agent RL with sparse rewards faces brittleness: dense intrinsic rewards alter underlying Markov game while world-model guidance amplifies model bias.
approach: SOLAR proposes simulate-evaluate-shape framework with learned world model enabling low-cost plateau testing; once plateau detected via statistical validation, injects potential-based shaping with uncertainty-aware throttling.
contribution: Provides theoretical analysis on policy invariance and plateau decision deviation; consistent gains in stability and final performance across sparse-reward offline MARL benchmarks with varying dataset quality.

problem: Private text generation methods via LLMs are severely inefficient: data-intensive, computationally slow, requiring large private corpora or batch sizes to achieve usable quality.
approach: EPSVec steers LLM generation using dataset vectors—directions in activation space capturing distributional gap—extracted once then used for standard decoding, enabling arbitrarily many samples without additional privacy cost.
contribution: Outperforms baselines in distributional alignment and downstream utility particularly in low-data regimes while significantly reducing computational overhead; differential privacy preserved throughout.

problem: Semantic watermarks embedding information in latent diffusion model noise are vulnerable to black-box forgery attacks, but existing methods lack rigorous theoretical understanding of attack conditions.
approach: Analyze attacks through rate-distortion lens in latent space, identifying irreducible distortion floor from structural proxy-target mismatches; characterize as structured geometric deviations (global drift and local deformation).
contribution: Propose scheme-agnostic detection distinguishing forged samples before verification; demonstrate effectiveness across diverse black-box scenarios while preserving robustness to common distortions.

problem: Discovering analytical solutions to differential equations requires expert intuition or exhaustive combinatorial search; data-driven approaches struggle with requiring large training data.
approach: SIGS uses context-free grammar generating mathematically valid blocks, embeds into topology-regularized continuous latent manifold, searches via structure selection then coefficient refinement against PDE residual and boundary conditions.
contribution: First neuro-symbolic method to recover analytical solutions for coupled nonlinear PDE systems and discover equivalent symbolic forms; improves over existing symbolic methods by orders of magnitude.

problem: Existing low-rank approximation for LLM compression focuses on minimizing individual layer output error without considering Transformer architecture, introducing runtime overhead from decomposed matrices.
approach: A3 splits Transformer layer into QK, OV, and MLP components, providing analytical solutions reducing hidden dimension size while minimizing component functional loss without introducing runtime overheads.
contribution: LLaMA 3.1-70B low-rank approximation achieves 4.69 perplexity on WikiText-2, outperforming sota 7.87; versatile applications in KV cache compression and quantization integration.

problem: Timestep embeddings in diffusion models are underexplored for security risks and malicious information injection despite containing substantial representational capacity.
approach: Shadow Timestep Embedding (STE) investigates temporal space for information injection, analyzing timestep embeddings as position-encoding with mutual coherence evaluation explaining separability of disjoint intervals.
contribution: Reveals timestep as powerful side channel for carrying dedicated information; timestep exhibits distinct representational capabilities encoding side-channel information usable for attack and defense.

problem: Large gap exists between best upper bound O(S^7 A^7) for replicable RL with exploration and O(S^2 A^2) for batch setting, raising questions whether replicable exploration is inherently expensive.
approach: Develop replicable RL algorithm on O(S^2 A) samples for low-horizon tabular MDPs by (nearly) resolving exploration-replicability interaction; complement with O(Ω(S^2)) lower bound.
contribution: Shows exploration is not significant barrier to replicable learning, nearly bridging gap between generative and episodic settings for sample-efficient replicable RL.
